unresolvedGap.issue: The official reference MCP filesystem server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem) provides read AND write tools (read_text_file, write_file, create_directory, move, etc.) with no built-in read-only flag found in its documentation.
unresolvedGap.decision: RESOLVED this cycle per the user's own stated preference order (read-only > scoped write > separate git worktree > isolated copy > unrestricted): created an isolated git worktree (`World_server AI\World_server_anythingllm_sandbox`, branch `ai/desktop/anythingllm-sandbox`) and scoped the filesystem MCP server to that worktree only, not the main World_server tree. A fresh `git worktree add` only materializes tracked files, so the sandbox is secret-free by construction (no `.env.local`/`WORLD_SERVER_SECRETS`) - a stronger guarantee than a denylist. This did NOT require the unrestricted-main-tree escalation question, because the worktree option fully satisfied the need without it.
unresolvedGap.verification: scripts/anythingllm-health-check.js flags any MCP filesystem server scoped to the literal main World_server path as unsafeMainTreeGrant=true (hard FAIL). test/anythingllm-mcp-secret-guard.test.js (4/4 PASS) proves both that a secret marker in a scoped directory is caught, and that a main-tree grant is flagged.
options: accept read+write MCP filesystem access for AnythingLLM (a real, deliberate risk tradeoff)
find/vet a read-only-capable filesystem MCP server or wrapper
defer live filesystem access for AnythingLLM and keep it scoped to RAG-ingested documents only, at least initially

toolCallingReliabilityFinding.conclusion: Neither thinking setting reliably completes an agentic tool-calling turn for qwen3:1.7b under current real CPU contention on this machine (observed 18%-100% load, driven by other concurrent AI-agent processes). This is a genuine, currently-unresolved model-capability/throughput limitation, not a routing or proxy defect - the deterministic router, MCP proxy, and reranker-narrowing fixes from the prior cycle are all independently verified working (see structural test counts). Recorded in error-prevention-registry.json and lib/model-suitability.js (qwen3:1.7b now correctly flagged unsuitable for filesystem-read: 100% fail rate over last 5 real attempts).
toolCallingReliabilityFinding.recommendation: qwen2.5:3b-instruct (or similar non-hybrid-thinking small instruct model with established Ollama tool-calling support) - see final integration report for full justification. Not downloaded without explicit approval.
toolCallingReliabilityFinding.supersededBy: trueRootCause below - this section's conclusion (a model-capability/throughput limitation) was itself wrong. Kept verbatim as an honest record of the investigation path, not deleted, per the explicit instruction to preserve eliminated hypotheses as diagnostic knowledge.

trueRootCause.finding: The empty-content/no-tool_calls defect was caused by scripts/anythingllm-task-router.cjs's OWN tool-name hint, not by CPU, model choice, thinking mode, tool count, or streaming.
trueRootCause.mechanism: The router's hint ("Use exactly one of these tools: list_directory, search_files, read_file, read_text_file...") named the SHORT/unprefixed tool names from lib/mcp-intent-router.js's allowedTools. AnythingLLM actually registers MCP tools under a PREFIXED name: <mcpServerName>-<toolName> (e.g. "world-server-sandbox-read_text_file", not "read_text_file"). Instructing the model to call a tool name that does not exist in its own declared tools list broke tool-call generation entirely.
trueRootCause.isolationMethod: Matrix test: replayed AnythingLLM's EXACT captured request (system prompt, tool schema, model, num_ctx) directly against raw Ollama, bypassing AnythingLLM and the proxy entirely, then bisected one variable at a time (tool count 1 vs 5, $schema field present/absent, short vs prefixed tool name, system prompt content, presence of the router's hint) until isolating a single controlled variable: WITHOUT the hint, hasToolCalls:true with the correct prefixed name; WITH the hint, hasToolCalls:false, empty content - identical everything else.
trueRootCause.fix: scripts/anythingllm-task-router.cjs#prefixedToolName() - both hint-construction sites now map allowed tool names through it before sending them to the model. See error-prevention-registry.json#anythingllm-router-hint-tool-name-mismatch.
trueRootCause.liveValidation: Confirmed via real AnythingLLM+Ollama backend log evidence (not just the isolated Ollama replay): a real world-server-sandbox-read_text_file tool call executed successfully and returned the exact correct package.json content (name: webgl-survival-hub-no-npm) through the full AnythingLLM pipeline after the fix.
secondaryFindingsKeptAsRealImprovements: stream:true vs stream:false: a real latency/reliability factor for long-running requests (Node's default http.Server requestTimeout=300000ms was silently killing genuinely-completing turns) - fixed in scripts/ollama-think-proxy.cjs, unrelated to the empty-content root cause.

Ollama model cold-load time under extreme system memory/disk pressure can reach many minutes (observed: 107 minutes for a trivial call) - now factored into lib/ai-resource-scheduler.js's dispatch decision via live /api/ps residency checks.
world-server-sandbox-search_files (recursive scan) measured a real MCP -32001 timeout on the ~2815-file sandbox tree - now deprioritized by lib/tool-cost-model.js in favor of targeted reads.
